summary: Prefix cache thrashing on repeat-context workloads causing intermittent 500-2000ms latency spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported sudden latency regressions for repeat prompts that historically completed within 60-120ms. Starting 2026-03-10 08:30 UTC TellCo observed intermittent tail latency spikes between ~500ms and ~2000ms for identical repeated prompts. Spikes coincide with a small increase in request volume and correlate with streaming and non-streaming requests to the same model instance set.

Impact:
- TellCo (dedicated tenant) reports elevated P50->P95 token latency and occasional request timeouts when sending sequences that reuse recent conversation prefixes.
- Customer workflows (real-time search summarization) degrade during spikes; several jobs retried by their client.
- No 5xx error rate spike at API layer, but internal timeouts observed in serving-runtime with increased latency.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool (customer-dedicated-gpu-pool-23) in us-west-2
- Model: redwood-rlm-7b-v1 pinned by customer
- Serving runtime version: 1.12.3
- Cache service version: 0.9.8

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Send a short chat-style prompt with ~120 tokens prefix and 3-4 token continuation.
2) Repeat same request 30-60 times at 30 QPS, mixing streaming and non-streaming calls.
3) Observe median latency ~80ms for initial runs, then intermittent runs with 600-1800ms and occasional client-side timeouts.

Observed logs / metrics excerpts:
- Serving runtime traces show long waits in cache-lookup path (key: prefix-hash) and increased mutex contention on cache shards.
- Cache eviction rate (items/sec) spikes concurrently with latency events.
- KV lookup histogram shifts to a long tail for "prefix-match" operations.
- No corresponding GPU utilization increase; CPU on cache service increases ~30% during spikes.

Initial hypothesis:
- Prefix cache thrashing due to high collision rate in prefix-hash buckets under mixed streaming/non-streaming access patterns.
- Eviction storms triggered by a small working set hitting set-associativity limits on the cache shard implementation, causing extra KV cache misses and repeated recomputation of KV prefix state.
- Continuous batching in serving runtime increases overlapped requests that touch similar prefixes but slightly different length boundaries, producing frequent near-identical prefix keys and causing churn.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Scoped a targeted routing rule to move TellCo traffic to a sibling cache shard group (manual shard affinity) at 2026-03-10 11:45 UTC which reduced tail latency for ~2 hours.
- Applied conservative per-tenant cache-ttl increase for prefix entries to reduce eviction frequency (rollback prepared).

Next steps (engineering):
- Eng to replicate with workload generator that alternates streaming/non-streaming and slightly perturbed prefix lengths (assigned to Omar).
- Instrument finer-grained cache shard metrics (per-bucket occupancy, associativity conflicts).
- Evaluate short-term engineering patch to increase associativity or change prefix hashing to reduce collisions.
- Consider adding request-level fallback to avoid repeated KV recompute if eviction storms detected.

Customer communication note:
- Customer notified at 2026-03-10 12:05 UTC with temporary mitigation and asked to validate. They have accepted the routing change but requested a permanent fix and postmortem.

investigation_notes: Reproducer notes: Using the customer's replay script we reproduced 95th percentile increase when mixing streaming and non-streaming requests that differ by 1-3 token prefix length. Root cause signal points to cache set-associativity exhaustion in hot buckets rather than logic bug in eviction policy. Patch candidate: increase associativity from 4->8 for prefix shards and widen hash to 64-bit to lower collision probability. Also evaluating short-term mitigation to add small randomized salt per request to spread load across buckets (careful: must preserve prefix equivalence when appropriate).
resolution: Work in progress. Temporary customer routing and TTL change applied; engineering patch PR opened to increase associativity and switch hash function. Planned rolling deploy for 2026-03-18 with canary in us-west-2. Postmortem to follow after deploy. Customer will be notified of timeline and final remediation.
